inner-glow.title: Inner Glow AI
inner-glow.intro: A mental health app that turns daily check-ins into one score people can understand, and gives a next step for every result.

Problem.label: 01 — PROBLEM
Problem.name: Problem
Problem.intro: People who want to look after their mental health usually start strong and stop after a week. Mood trackers collect data but don't explain it, meditation apps don't know how you feel today, and therapy is expensive with long waiting lists. The result is a lot of logging and no clear answer to: am I getting better, and what should I do today?
Problem.text: People who want to look after their mental health usually start strong and stop after a week. Mood trackers collect data but don't explain it, meditation apps don't know how you feel today, and therapy is expensive with long waiting lists. The result is a lot of logging and no clear answer to: am I getting better, and what should I do today?
Problem.hmw: How might we help people understand their mental state in seconds and give them one small, useful action every day?

Research.label: 02 — RESEARCH
Research.name: Research
Research.finding: Main finding: people stopped because the app felt like homework, the charts didn’t tell them anything, and paid content appeared before any value.

Audience.label: 03 — AUDIENCE
Audience.name: Audience
Audience.intro: Who the site is for, what each group needs, and the page that answers it.

personas.name: Venue operators
texts: “I don’t have time for another app.”
A check-in that takes seconds, not minutes.

personas.name: Investors & developers
texts: “Why am I so tired all week?”
To see how sleep, mood and stress connect.

personas.name: Public sector clients
texts: “I need something until I get help.”
Safe support and a clear route to a professional.

Journey map.label: 04 — JOURNEY MAP
Journey map.name: Journey map
Journey map.intro: What a visitor does, thinks and struggles with at each step, and the design decision that answers it.

rows.label: DESIGN RESPONSE
cells: Mood, sleep, stress and AI in one app
Value first, upgrade after real use

Hypotheses.label: 05 — HYPOTHESES
Hypotheses.name: Hypotheses
Hypotheses.intro: Eight hypotheses, each with its own metric, ordered by priority. Drawn as variants of one component: same structure, different bet.
items: One 0–100 score is easier to follow than separate mood, sleep and stress charts.
A short assessment at the start makes the first result feel personal.
3–4 suggested actions after each score turn logging into action.
A one-tap emoji check-in keeps daily logging under 30 seconds.
Clear AI framing, with a route to a real professional, makes people trust the chat.
Weekly chat use, support link taps
Smart reminders based on the user’s own patterns work better than fixed daily pings.
Optional voice input helps people who find it hard to put feelings into words.
Showing paid features after real use converts better than a paywall after onboarding.

Prioritisation.label: 06 — PRIORITISATION
Prioritisation.name: Prioritisation
Prioritisation.intro: Each hypothesis placed by expected impact and the effort to build it. The score went first even as a big bet: every other feature depends on it.

Visitor flow.label: 07 — VISITOR FLOW
Visitor flow.name: Visitor flow
Visitor flow.intro: The daily loop and the support path. Both end with one next step: an action, an exercise or a link to a professional.

Sitemap.label: 08 — SITEMAP
Sitemap.name: Sitemap
Sitemap.intro: Five tabs: Home, Practices, Journal and Profile, with Glow AI in the central button.

Wireframes to UI.label: 09 — WIREFRAMES TO UI
Wireframes to UI.name: Wireframes to UI
Wireframes to UI.intro: Low-fidelity layout first, agreed with the client, then the final interface.

Solution.label: 10 — SOLUTION
Solution.name: Solution
notes: Assessment
14 questions, one per screen, with a progress counter and a skip option on sensitive topics.
InnerGlow Score
One number from 0 to 100 with a plain-language label, and a history of what changed.
AI suggestions
3–4 actions after each score — mindfulness, activity, social, professional support — with time needed.
Mood check-in
One tap with 5 emoji states and an optional note. 12 seconds on average in testing.
AI companion
Text and voice chat with clear limits. Support contacts always sit in the chat header.
Trade-off
A single score can feel reductive, so details stay one tap away and every score has a label in words.

What we measure.label: 12 — WHAT WE MEASURE
What we measure.name: What we measure
What we measure.intro: Eight hypotheses across five stages of the journey. Targets were set before launch; the prototype test already gave a first signal for four of the five stages.
table: Weekly opens of score history; actions completed weekly
5 of 6 called actions the most useful part
Weekly chat use, support link taps
2 of 6 missed support contacts CHANGED THE DESIGN Moved into the chat header
Notification opt-out, share of voice entries, trial start, day-7 retention

Results.label: 13 — RESULTS
Results.name: Results
cols: Tested as a prototype

Moderated sessions with 6 people on Maze. 6 of 6 finished onboarding and understood their first score without help. The mood check-in took 12 seconds on average, and 5 of 6 said the suggested actions were the most useful part. Two people missed the support contacts, so they moved into the chat header.
What I would do next

In mental health products, tone matters as much as layout: “difficult day” instead of “negative” changed how people read the same chart. Next: test a shorter 5-question assessment, then track day-2 and day-7 retention and weekly suggested actions.

jbc.title: JBC Projects
jbc.intro: A website that answers one question for venue owners: has this firm delivered a project like mine?

Problem.label: 01 — PROBLEM
Problem.name: Problem
Problem.intro: JBC's clients are venue owners, operators and investors planning large, long-term projects. Before they get in touch, they check one thing: has this firm delivered a project like mine? The firm's experience was not presented in one clear place, so the answer was hard to find.
Problem.text: JBC's clients are venue owners, operators and investors planning large, long-term projects. Before they get in touch, they check one thing: has this firm delivered a project like mine? The firm's experience was not presented in one clear place, so the answer was hard to find.
Problem.hmw: How might we help visitors confirm JBC’s experience in one visit and make contacting the firm the obvious next step?

Research.label: 02 — RESEARCH
Research.name: Research
Research.finding: Main finding: clients choose a venue consultant on its past projects and clients first. The service list comes second.

What I would do next

For B2B services, clear project information matters more than visual effects. Next: filter projects by venue type, add capacity and opening year to project cards, and add a project-stage field to the enquiry form.

dalitis.title: Andreas Dalitis & Sons
dalitis.intro: One website for three audiences: homebuyers, investors and businesses — and a reason to trust a new development.

Problem.label: 01 — PROBLEM
Problem.name: Problem
Problem.intro: The audience is wide: homebuyers, investors and businesses looking for commercial space. A buyer wants to see what is for sale now, an investor wants proof of past projects, a business wants to know if the company can build for them. The site had to answer all three without clutter.
Problem.text: The audience is wide: homebuyers, investors and businesses looking for commercial space. A buyer wants to see what is for sale now, an investor wants proof of past projects, a business wants to know if the company can build for them. The site had to answer all three without clutter.
Problem.hmw: How might we help each visitor find what is relevant to them quickly, and turn interest in a development into an enquiry?

Research.label: 02 — RESEARCH
Research.name: Research
Research.finding: Main finding: visitors look for a specific development first and read about the company second. Trust comes from finished buildings, not long text.

thallo.title: Thallo Building
thallo.intro: Selling 2,068 m² of green office space in Larnaca before the building exists.

Problem.label: 01 — PROBLEM
Problem.name: Problem
Problem.intro: Thallo is still under construction, so there is no finished building to show. Companies looking for an office need to picture the space, understand what they can rent and decide if it is worth a viewing — all from renders and plans.
Problem.text: Thallo is still under construction, so there is no finished building to show. Companies looking for an office need to picture the space, understand what they can rent and decide if it is worth a viewing — all from renders and plans.
Problem.hmw: How might we help a company understand the building and the available space in one visit, and make booking a viewing the natural next step?

Research.label: 02 — RESEARCH
Research.name: Research
Research.finding: Main finding: companies choosing an office look for hard facts first — size, location, features, completion date. Clear numbers beat lifestyle text.

pcela.title: Pcela Flower
pcela.intro: A flower shop where a gift for someone else is ordered on a phone in a few minutes.

Problem.label: 01 — PROBLEM
Problem.name: Problem
Problem.intro: Most people buy flowers in a hurry: a birthday, a date, an apology. They open the site on a phone and want to choose a bouquet, a time and an address in minutes. Many orders go to another person, sometimes anonymously — and the range is wide.
Problem.text: Most people buy flowers in a hurry: a birthday, a date, an apology. They open the site on a phone and want to choose a bouquet, a time and an address in minutes. Many orders go to another person, sometimes anonymously — and the range is wide.
Problem.hmw: How might we help someone find the right bouquet and send it to another person quickly, on a phone, without calling the shop?

Research.label: 02 — RESEARCH
Research.name: Research
Research.finding: Main finding: customers decide by photo and delivery time, not by descriptions. Most order for someone else and worry about timing and the recipient’s details.

Audience.name: Audience
Audience.intro: Who the site is for, what each group needs, and the page that answers it.

notes: Three promises
Delivery in 90 minutes, a freshness guarantee, a gift box and bag from 10,000 ₽.
Online showcase
Ready bouquets delivered in 90 minutes, then bestsellers and categories: premium, mono, baskets, WOW sets.
Add-ons in the cart

Order form
